vocab.definition: the volume of one mole of any gas at rtp = 24 dm³.
equal volumes of gases have equal moles (same conditions).

misconceptions.wrong: Heavier gases take up more volume.
misconceptions.right: At rtp, one mole of ANY gas is 24 dm³.
It only applies at room temperature and pressure.

misconceptions.wrong: cm³ and dm³ are the same.
misconceptions.right: Divide cm³ by 1000 to get dm³.

infoPanels.title: GAS VOLUME AT rtp
infoPanels.content: 1 mole of gas = 24 dm³ at rtp

questions.text: Calculate the moles in 48 dm³ of CO₂ at rtp. [2 marks]
Calculate the volume of 0.5 mol of O₂ at rtp. [2 marks]
Calculate the volume of 8 g of CH₄ at rtp. (Mᵣ = 16) [3 marks]
Explain why 1 mol of H₂ and 1 mol of CO₂ have the same volume at rtp. [1 mark]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: At rtp, one mole of any gas occupies ______ dm³, so volume ÷ 24 gives ______.

questions.text: 2 mol of gas is produced. Calculate the total gas volume at rtp. [1 mark]

footer.tip: At rtp: moles = volume (dm³) ÷ 24. Convert cm³ to dm³ first.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does the type of gas not change the volume of one mole at rtp?
